explanation: The least common multiple clears each truncated logarithm coefficient. Shift by a Gaussian integer and multiply by a natural number, take powers using d_i≤e_i, then multiply the cleared factors and extract a coefficient.
natural_language_statement:
Let $S$ be a finite index set; let $T_i,q_i,e_i,d_i$ be natural numbers, $z_i\in\mathbb Z[\mathrm i]$, and $P\in\mathbb Z[\mathrm i][X]$. Assume $d_i\le e_i$ for $i\in S$. Write $L_i=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,T_i)$ and $\ell_{T_i}(X)$ for the order-$T_i$ polynomial truncation of $\log(1+X)$. For every natural $k$,

$$\left(\prod_{i\in S}L_i^{e_i}\right)[X^k]\left(P(X)\prod_{i\in S}(z_i+q_i\ell_{T_i}(X))^{d_i}\right)\in\mathbb Z[\mathrm i]\subset\mathbb C.$$

This is the exact coefficient-integrality statement used to clear denominators in the interpolation matrix entries.

source_witness.mathematical_role: Clears all truncated-logarithm denominators and places the shifted product coefficient in the Gaussian-integer lattice used by the interpolation-matrix arithmetic bounds.

theorem_title: Gaussian integrality of cleared shifted logarithm product coefficients
